o: A bowl is a subarray of length >= 3 whose interior maximum is strictly below both endpoints. Key structural fact: with a decreasing monotonic stack of 'visible from the right' indices, when processing r we pop every stack element smaller than nums[r]; each popped element m forms a bowl (l, r) with l the element just below m on the stack, because everything between l and r is below nums[m] < nums[r]. If nothing is popped, the current top itself forms a bowl with r when the gap is at least 2. This counts every bowl exactly once, by its right endpoint.
k: For a fixed right end r, valid left ends are exactly the indices visible from r (previous-greater chain) whose next-visible value is < nums[r].
Monotonic stack pops enumerate these pairs: each pop of m pairs (element below m, r); if no pop occurs, the surviving top pairs with r.
Enforce length >= 3 by requiring r - l >= 2.

a.i: Keep a stack of indices with strictly decreasing values; every element between consecutive stack entries is smaller than the upper entry. When r pops m, the interior max of (l, r) — l just below m — equals nums[m] < nums[r], and nums[l] > nums[m], so it is a bowl. If no pop happens, the top t satisfies the same property directly.
s: Iterate r over the array maintaining the decreasing stack of indices.
While the top value < nums[r]: if a second element exists below and r - that index >= 2, count a bowl; pop.
If no element was popped and the stack is nonempty with r - top >= 2, count a bowl.
a.t: O(n) — each index is pushed and popped at most once.

w: Trace example 1 ([2,5,3,1,4]): at r=4 the pops of 1 and 3 yield bowls (2,4) and (1,4). Trace example 2: three no-pop/top bowls with l=0. Pitfalls: double counting the final top after pops (only count it when nothing was popped), and the length >= 3 gap check on the correct index (the element below the popped one). Follow-up: count 'peak' subarrays (both ends smaller than interior max) with a symmetric stack argument.
